claim: The internal doc asserts that `is_not_null` is generated as `NOT (x IS NULL)` so it keeps its meaning even if `HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE` were set, and that the unlisted link table and the `parent_rule` parent are in `CompiledRule.tables` so the guard's prefix choice and model-CTE renaming cover them as they cover every other table a filter reads.
source_excerpt: `is_null` compiles to `exp.Is(column, exp.Null())` and `is_not_null` to `exp.Not(exp.Paren(exp.Is(...)))`, generated as `NOT (x IS NULL)` so it keeps its meaning even if `HIGH_NOT_PRECEDENCE` were set. A `parent_rule` is compiled at the parent's slot and AND-ed beside the parent's own rule inside the same `EXISTS`, so both test one parent row; an unlisted link table gets no own-rule condition. The unlisted link table and the `parent_rule` parent are in `CompiledRule.tables`, so the guard's prefix choice and model-CTE renaming cover them as they cover every other table a filter reads.
verify_against: `_Compiler._node` and `_new_slot` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py`, and the CTE renaming in `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py`
verify_hint: Check `_Compiler._node`'s `IsNotNullRule`, `InheritRule` and `ReferencedByRule` branches and `_new_slot` in `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py`
